item.title: Casa Amona / COLAR Colectivo de Arquitectura
item.dc:creator: Valentina Díaz
item.description: The project is located on an urban lot in San Cristóbal de las Casas, adjacent to one of the city's main green areas. The house maintains a restrained relationship with the street, focusing its daily life toward the interior of the property, where various openings and courtyards establish visual connections with both the surrounding landscape and the home's internal spaces.

item.title: CASA ÂNCORA / Tiago Sousa
item.dc:creator: Andreas Luco
item.description: A remote, rugged and serene place, marked by the contrast between heat and cold.

item.title: Ellen Browning Building / Hacker Architects
item.dc:creator: Andreas Luco
item.description: The genesis for the mixed-use residential Ellen Browning Building arose when a group of close friends considered how they could preserve their relationships during their last years. Co-housing, with its spirit of community and shared living spaces, provided the answer. By developing their own residential building, the friends would be able to balance togetherness with the independence of urban living. The site they selected is set within a vibrant retail and commercial district along Division Street in Southeast Portland. Like many seniors, choosing to live in a walkable, amenity-supported and health-care rich city is an aging-in-place strategy.

item.title: The Gallery House / Maden Architects
item.dc:creator: Nina Vuga
item.description: "The Gallery" is conceived as a contemporary residence where architecture, natural light, movement, and landscape come together to create a calm and refined living experience. The project is inspired by the idea of architecture as a continuous journey rather than a collection of separate spaces. Clean geometric volumes establish a strong architectural identity, while carefully framed openings, courtyards, and landscaped areas create a constant visual and spatial relationship between the interior and its natural surroundings.

item.title: The Forum Installation 2027 Open Call for Site-Responsive Installations
item.dc:creator: Rene Submissions
item.description:
The Forum at Fabrik invites students and emerging designers to propose a temporary spatial installation for a prominent public-facing site in the Gaslight District, one of Cambridge's emerging cultural and urban destinations.

Created to support the next generation of designers, the program provides an opportunity to take an idea beyond drawings and models—to design, build, and present a full-scale work within an active public setting.

Up to three proposals will be selected and realized sequentially over the course of one year. Each selected project will receive:

Up to $4,500 CAD in project support to realize the installation
A $500 CAD honorarium through The FORUM

item.title: Call for Abstracts: 2027 Modern Conversation Conference on Education
item.dc:creator: Rene Submissions
item.description:
Join our upcoming annual edition of “modern conversations”, where we examine spaces of pedagogy to analyze the shifting terrains of educational practices, institutions, and environments that influence the creation and dissemination of knowledge. This inquiry prompts us to consider: where does learning occur, both historically and in the contemporary world? What is the connection between modernity and education? In what ways has modernity transformed educational spaces? When did education adopt a formal structure, and how was this reflected spatially? How have socio-political dynamics shaped these environments? Most crucially, why is it critical to examine the spaces where education happens?

item.title: Open Call: Urban design competition for the Kłodnica Boulevards in Gliwice
item.dc:creator: Rene Submissions
item.description: The City of Gliwice invites entries for a one-stage urban planning, landscape, and architectural design competition to develop a development concept for the Kłodnica Boulevards in Gliwice. The goal of the competition is to obtain a high-quality urban planning, landscape, and architectural concept for the Kłodnica River valley within the city limits of Gliwice. We are seeking visionary solutions that will transform the riverside corridor into a vibrant, multifunctional public space, integrate urban green spaces into a cohesive natural system, create safe walking and biking routes, and strengthen the city’s resilience to climate change.

item.title: Oris Day
item.dc:creator: Rene Submissions
item.description:
The Oris Day architectural symposium takes place on Sunday, 8 November 2026, in Zagreb, at the Mozaik Event Centre.
The central programme will bring together this year’s Pritzker Prize laureate Smiljan Radić Clarke and Swiss architect Christian Kerez. The audience will have the opportunity to follow their conversation live – a dialogue between two distinguished architects about architecture, the creative process and contemporary challenges facing the profession.

item.title: RE_SOLUTION: Fernando Medina, former Mayor of Lisbon, at IE School of Architecture & Design
item.dc:creator: Rene Submissions
item.description:
IE School of Architecture & Design (IE University) will launch the 2026–27 edition of its RE_SOLUTION public series with a lecture by Fernando Medina, Mayor of Lisbon from 2015 to 2021, followed by a conversation with Jo da Silva, Global Director of Sustainable Development at Arup.

RE_SOLUTION brings together former city leaders and experts to examine how cities respond to complex urban challenges through public infrastructure, transformative projects, policy, and collaboration across government, the private sector, academia, and civil society.

item.title: Festival des Architectures Vives
item.dc:creator: Rene Submissions
item.description:
Festival des Architectures Vives 2027 in Montpellier: Call for Applications

The Festival des Architectures Vives (FAV) has launched its call for applications for its 21st edition, taking place in Montpellier, France, from 15 to 20 June 2027. Under the theme “Shared Happiness”, the festival invites young professionals in architecture, landscape architecture, urban planning and related disciplines to design temporary installations for the historic courtyards of Montpellier’s private mansions.

Applications are open until 7 December 2026.

item.title: Anthology ASEAN Architecture Festival
item.dc:creator: Rene Submissions
item.description:
Anthology ASEAN Architecture Festival 2026: Shared Ground
Architecture of Care, Culture, and Collective Futures
October 2–4, 2026 · Intramuros, Manila, Philippines

I. Leading ASEAN Voices in Architecture is coming to Intramuros for Shared Ground

Ground, in Southeast Asia, has never been neutral. It bends under monsoon rain, shifts with reclaimed coastlines, and carries the layered memory of settlements, colonial grids, and postwar cities built one on top of another. This is the premise the Anthology ASEAN Architecture Festival 2026 opens with: that the terrain our region builds on is shared, climatically, historically, and socially, whether we choose to acknowledge it or not.

item.title: Frank Gehry - Illuminations
item.dc:creator: Rene Submissions
item.description: Frank Gehry – Illuminations is a conference and workshop programme held in Istanbul as part of Architecture Week, organised by the Istanbul Association of Architects in Private Practice (İstanbulSMD) in memory of the late Frank Gehry.

item.title: From Seasonal Escape to Permanent Elsewhere: Movement and Architecture in the Gulf
item.dc:creator: Ananya Nayak
item.description: For many communities across the Gulf, leaving home once formed part of inhabiting it. Families moved between desert pastures, coastal settlements, wells, fishing grounds, and pearling ports according to season and livelihood, returning repeatedly to places already known through use. In Qatar, historical accounts describe autumn and winter movement through al-barr, the desert, followed by a return toward coastal settlements as the summer pearling season began. The National Museum of Qatar represents this history through a yearly calendar of movement between desert and sea.

item.title: Trinity College Lawson Centre for Sustainability / Mecanoo + RDHA
item.dc:creator: Pilar Caballero
item.description: The Lawson Centre for Sustainability is Trinity College's most ambitious capital project in over six decades and one of Canada's most advanced sustainability-driven academic and residential buildings. Designed by Dutch architecture firm Mecanoo, working in collaboration with Toronto architecture firm RDHA, the Lawson Centre revitalizes Trinity's beautiful campus, enhances the collegiate experience for students and embodies the College's commitment to sustainability.

item.title: Accelerating Architectural Design: Lessons From Bellway
item.dc:creator: Rene Submissions
item.description: As architectural projects grow more complex and requirements evolve, the ability to iterate quickly is increasingly important to the design process. For Bellway, one of the UK's largest homebuilders, faster design iteration and visualization have become key to meeting these demands. It is not just a way to present finished designs, but also a tool for testing ideas, communicating options, and making decisions earlier in the development process.

item.title: African Futures Institute Transforms Former Warehouse Into Headquarters in Accra, Ghana
item.dc:creator: Reyyan Dogan
item.description: The African Futures Institute (AFI) has completed its new headquarters in Accra, Ghana, transforming a former tile warehouse in the city's Osu neighbourhood into a centre for architectural education, research, exhibitions, and public programmes. The project retains the existing industrial structure while introducing spaces for teaching, workshops, performances, screenings, and gatherings. Its completion gives the Institute a permanent base in Accra after several years of operating through programmes, partnerships, and temporary spaces across Africa and beyond.

item.title: Floating Sauna / DinellJohansson
item.dc:creator: Cristina Popescu
item.description: At the end of October 2025, the historic but dilapidated Liljeholmsbadet was towed away permanently. It is to be renovated and subsequently relocated across the water to Marievik.

item.title: MAD Architects' Lucas Museum of Narrative Art Opens to the Public in Los Angeles
item.dc:creator: Antonia Piñeiro
item.description: The Lucas Museum of Narrative Art officially opens its doors to the public today, September 22, 2026. The museum's sculptural, curved silhouette was designed by Ma Yansong of MAD Architects, with landscape architecture by Mia Lehrer of Studio-MLA and Stantec serving as executive architect. The opening follows a Founding Members Preview held from September 5 to 11, giving members an exclusive early look at the galleries, and a star-studded opening night on Saturday, September 19, featuring celebrity co-chairs at a launch event for the museum, co-founded by George Lucas and Mellody Hobson. The date aligns with the announcement made by the institution nearly a year ago, though the project has a longer history: approved in 2017, with construction beginning the following year, the opening was originally planned for 2025. The museum sits within an 11-acre (4.5-hectare) site in Los Angeles's Exposition Park and comprises a 300,000-square-foot (27,900-square-meter) structure featuring galleries, two theaters, a retail store, a library, a café, a restaurant, and event spaces.

item.title: Steel Architectural Awards ASEAN 2026 Announces 12 Finalists Advancing Regional Design Excellence
item.dc:creator: Rene Submissions
item.description: The Steel Architectural Awards ASEAN 2026, presented by BlueScope, has announced the 12 finalist projects selected to advance to the ASEAN-level appraisal. Representing outstanding achievements in architecture across Indonesia, Malaysia, Thailand, and Vietnam, the finalists were selected through the Country Awards programs and now move forward to regional evaluation by an international judging panel.

item.title: Built to Exclude: Colonial Violence and Urban Ecologies in Africa
item.dc:creator: Maisa Elamein
item.description: Colonial violence in African cities bled through the political dimensions into the spatial realm. It is infused into street grids, land tenure systems, drainage infrastructure and residential zones that continue to organize inequality and displacement today. Kinshasa, Khartoum, and Kampala each carry this afterlife in their urban morphology, at once historical artifacts and an active structure; shaping who has access to services, who occupies flood-prone land, and catalyzing a deepening climate instability that forces this apparatus into entirely new dimensions - including geological ones.

item.title: The Kemilau Ubud / PSA Studio
item.dc:creator: Miwa Negoro
item.description: Kemilau Ubud is designed to recreate the sensation of exploring a tropical forest through dense landscapes and flowing rivers, represented by an organically designed swimming pool that winds through the trees. Each architectural element is carefully considered to blend harmoniously with the environment, creating an immersive and natural spatial experience. The design approach emphasizes sustainability through the use of natural materials such as wood, stone, and local vegetation, which are left in their natural state without excessive finishing. This allows the inherent expression of the materials to become an integral part of the space's character.

item.title: The Sayla Hotel / EKAR Architects
item.dc:creator: Pratik Mour
item.description: "Nimmana Haeminda" is a community in which a small guest house of "Baan Sayla" is located. The community used to combine distinct characters of local residents, namely, merchants, teachers, and a mix of creatives and artists through generations.

item.title: Haikou Workers’ Activity Center (Workers’ Cultural Palace) / CADG
item.dc:creator: Valeria Silva
item.description: Located on Hainan Island, Haikou is characterized by a hot and humid coastal climate. Designed by the Green Architecture Design & Research Institute of CADG, the newly completed Haikou Workers' Activity Center is conceived around the concept of "Tree of Life" and organized as an "Ecological Settlement," setting a new benchmark for climate-responsive public architecture in Haikou. More than a civic complex integrating cultural, sports, and training programs, the project creates an urban oasis—community-oriented, climate-responsive, and low-carbon in operation.

item.title: La Haya House / PH TIPO CASA
item.dc:creator: Valentina Díaz
item.description: Parque Chas presents us with multiple residential typologies. This project sits on an almost square lot, a renovation originally carried out in the 2000s on a traditional "casa cajón" (box house).
